item.title: The Strange Story of America’s First “Alien Abduction”
item.author: Weird History
item.content:encoded:
During a late-night drive through rural New Hampshire in 1961, Barney and Betty Hill reported a terrifying encounter with a UFO that would change their lives forever. Since then, their story remains one of the most famous and controversial alien abduction cases in history. From unexplained missing time and hypnotic regression to eerie eyewitness testimony, the Hills' account helped shape modern beliefs about extraterrestrials, UFO sightings, and even the mysteries surrounding Area 51. But were they telling the truth, or did something else happen that night?
In this episode of Weird History Presents: Graveyard Shift, we explore the shocking details behind America's first widely publicized alien abduction case, the evidence that still fuels debate decades later, and why the Barney and Betty Hill story continues to captivate believers and skeptics alike.
Do you think it's possible that the Hills were really abducted by aliens? Let us know in the comments!

item.title: The End Of America’s Most Dangerous Amusement Park | Last Days
item.author: Weird History
item.content:encoded:
New Jersey's Action Park, the world's most infamous water park, closed its doors in 1996. It eventually reopened as Mountain Creek Waterpark, but in 2014 the son of the original owner brought back the legendary Action Park name. His goal was simple: recreate the thrill that made the original park famous, just without the injuries, lawsuits, and deadly reputation. But reviving America's most dangerous amusement park proved far more complicated than anyone expected.
LAST DAYS is Weird History’s prestige format series focusing on final chapters, deaths, downfalls and conclusions. In this episode, we examine the shocking true story behind Action Park's controversial comeback, the accidents that defined its legacy, and why the park's final chapter ended in failure.
(Much like real history, this video was produced entirely by human beings.)

item.content:encoded: Правда ли, что скорость света — не абсолютный предел, путешествия во времени могут оказаться возможными, а некоторые из самых популярных теорий современной физики вообще невозможно проверить?В новом выпуске — разговор с Сабиной Хоссенфельдер, физиком-теоретиком, доктором наук и одним из самых известных научных популяризаторов в мире. Мы обсудили главные загадки современной физики: происхождение Вселенной, природу времени, возможность существования внеземных цивилизаций, искусственный интеллект, свободу воли и теории, которые сегодня вызывают больше всего споров среди ученых.— Почему скорость света может быть не пределом для передачи информации?— Почему человечество может искать инопланетные цивилизации совершенно не там?— Возможны ли путешествия во времени с точки зрения современной физики?— Почему свобода воли может оказаться иллюзией?— Может ли искусственный интеллект когда-нибудь стать по-настоящему разумным?— Живем ли мы внутри компьютерной симуляции?— Почему мультивселенную невозможно доказать?— Что на самом деле известно о Большом взрыве и первом моменте существования Вселенной?— Почему Сабина считает многие современные космологические теории скорее математическими историями, чем наукой?▶︎ Телеграм-канал Глеба Соломина: https://t.me/gleb_solomin

item.title: The chemotherapy-induced senescence-associated secretome promotes cell detachment and metastatic dissemination through metabolic reprogramming
item.author: Katherine M. Aird
item.content:encoded: Cole and colleagues identify fructose as a component of the secretome in therapy-induced senescent ovarian cancer cells that drives metastasis. Fructose metabolically reprograms neighboring cancer cells, enhancing their ability to detach by reducing plasma membrane cholesterol through modulation of complex I and NAD.

item.title: Agentic AI for scaling diagnosis and care in neurodegenerative disease
item.author: Pedro Pinheiro-Chagas
item.content:encoded: In this Perspective, the authors envision that agentic AI systems may in the future support clinical workflows for neurodegenerative disease diagnosis and care. They propose a system for scaling specialist-level dementia care via synergistic collaborations between humans and an AI-driven continuously learning healthcare system that can reason across all patient data.

item.title: Plasma proteomics framework predicts metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease up to 16 years before onset
item.author: Hao Chen
item.content:encoded: Using plasma proteomics, Yu, Chen, Feng, Li et. al report a panel of five blood proteins that can predict future risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) up to 16 years before clinical onset, offering a potential tool for early risk stratification.

item.title: Ultra-early proteomic signatures predict MASLD up to 16 years ahead
item.content:encoded: A plasma proteomic signature enables accurate prediction of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) up to 16 years before diagnosis, and offers a clinically applicable proteomic framework for early risk stratification and preventive intervention.

item.content:encoded:
For centuries, eyewitnesses have claimed to spot a massive, mysterious beast gliding through the depths of Scotland's Loch Ness. Scientists, explorers, and monster hunters have spent decades searching for evidence, using everything from sonar scans to underwater expeditions, yet the truth remains as elusive as ever.
In this episode of Weird History Presents: Graveyard Shift, we dive into the legend of the Loch Ness Monster, exploring its ancient origins, the most famous sightings, shocking investigations, alleged hoaxes, and the enduring mystery that continues to captivate millions around the world. Is Nessie a prehistoric creature lurking beneath the dark waters of the loch? Or one of history's greatest hoaxes?

item.title: Red gold: The world's most expensive spice - Carolyn Beans
item.author: TED-Ed
item.content:encoded:
Dig into the unique biology of saffron and trace humanity’s enduring obsession with the spice, dating back thousands of years.
--
Spices are often far pricier proportionately than the foods they flavor. But one’s cost has long topped them all. Saffron’s red threads regularly run at rates of over 600 USD an ounce. So what is this so-called “red gold,” and what makes it so expensive? Carolyn Beans digs into the unique biology of saffron and humanity's enduring obsession with the spice.

item.title: Why The Most Dangerous Men Were Terrifed Of Griselda Blanco
item.author: Weird History
item.content:encoded:
Most people picture gangsters as powerful men in sharp suits, surrounded by cigar smoke, luxury, and violence. But one of the most feared crime bosses in history was a woman… and she was so ruthless that even Pablo Escobar was afraid of her.
On this episode of Weird History, we examine the shocking true story of the infamous "Queen of Cocaine," her rise to power, her brutal empire, and the legacy that made her one of the most dangerous figures in organized crime history.
Are you impressed that a woman could be such a powerful gangster? Let us know in the comments.
(Much like real history, this video was made entirely by human beings.)
